content: 1. Valeriane Leroy from the University of Bordeaux and Inserm U897-ISPED in France declared no conflicts of interest. 2. Mary Lou Lindgren from Boston University and Children’s Hospital in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 3. Divya Mallampati, a consultant at Northwestern University in the United States, declared no conflicts of interest. 4. Peter MacPherson from the University of Liverpool in the United Kingdom received financial support through a Wellcome Trust Clinical PhD Fellowship (2009–2010) and an Academy of Medical Sciences Clinical Lecturer Starter Grant (2014–2017). He declared significant financial institutional research support. 5. Susan Mallett from the University of Birmingham and Enhance Reviews Ltd in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 6. Edward Mills from Global Evaluative Sciences in Canada declared no conflicts of interest. 7. Jason Nagata from Stanford University School of Medicine in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 8. Matthew Neilson from the University of Sheffield in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 9. Eleanor Ochodon from Stellenbosch University and Enhance Reviews Ltd in South Africa declared no conflicts of interest. 10. Amy Penn from the University of California, San Francisco, in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 11. Marta Prescott from the Clinton Health Access Initiative in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 12. Jay Rajan from the University of California, San Francisco, in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 13. Sydney Rosen from Boston University in the United States declared employment as a full-time professor with research related to the project. She also served as the principal investigator for several research grants funded by USAID, the United States National Institutes of Health, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Travel to meetings was funded by these organizations and WHO. She declared significant financial and non-financial institutional research support. 14. George Rutherford from the University of California, San Francisco, declared travel to Geneva for a Clinical Guideline Development Group meeting, funded by Itad Ltd under a contract with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria. This was deemed financially non-significant. 15. Karla Soares-Weiser from Enhance Reviews Ltd in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 16. M. Eugenia Socias from Global Evaluative Sciences in Argentina declared no conflicts of interest. 17. Amitabh Suhtar, a consultant for WHO in Vietnam, declared no conflicts of interest. 18. Kelly Taylor from the University of California, San Francisco, in the United States declared no conflicts of interest. 19. Olalekan Uthman from Global Evaluative Sciences and Warwick Medical School in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 20. Brittany Urick from the Clinton Health Access Initiative in Kenya declared no conflicts of interest. 21. Lara Vojnov from the Clinton Health Access Initiative in Tanzania declared no conflicts of interest. 22. Matthew Wiens from Global Evaluative Sciences in Canada declared no conflicts of interest. 23. Taryn Young from Enhance Reviews Ltd and Stellenbosch University in South Africa declared no conflicts of interest. 24. Paul Garner from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom is the director of a DFID-funded research program focused on effective healthcare based on reliable research summaries. He declared non-financial significant support. 25. Timothy Hallett from Imperial College in the United Kingdom received financial support from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the World Bank, and other institutions, totaling $20,000 over two years. He also received $8 million in institutional support from UNAIDS, RUSH Research, and others. He declared significant financial support. 26. Anthony Harries from the International Union Against TB and Lung Disease in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 27. Salim Abdool Karim from CAPRISA in South Africa holds a patent for the effect of tenofovir gel on HSV. This was deemed non-financially significant. 28. Yogan Pillay from the Department of Health in South Africa declared no conflicts of interest. 29. Rebecca Matheson from ICW in Kenya declared no conflicts of interest. 30. Fabio Mesquita from the Department of STDs, AIDS, and Viral Hepatitis in Brazil declared no conflicts of interest. 31. Julio Montaner from the University of British Columbia in Canada received institutional grants from the British Columbia Ministry of Health and pharmaceutical companies such as AbbVie, Gilead Sciences, and others. He also received financial support from organizations like WHO, UNAIDS, and UNICEF. He declared significant financial support. 32. Natalia Nizova from the Ukraine Centre for Social Disease Control declared no conflicts of interest. 33. Douglas Shaffer from the Office of the United States Global AIDS Coordinator declared no conflicts of interest. 34. Nandi Siegfried, an independent clinical epidemiologist from South Africa, consulted as a methodologist for WHO from 2011 to 2015, receiving remuneration exceeding $40,000. This was deemed financially non-significant. 35. Kenly Sikwese from the African Community Advisory Board (AFROCAB) in Zambia received grants for community consultation from ViiV Healthcare, Gilead, and Janssen, totaling $30,000 and $35,000. AFROCAB is seeking further financial support from these organizations. This was deemed financially significant. 36. David Sinclair from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 37. Annette Sohn from TREAT Asia/amfAR in Thailand received research and training grants for her institution. Medicine donations for a hepatitis C research study were provided to the research unit only. This was deemed financially significant. 38. Stefano Vella from Istituto Superiore di Sanità in Italy declared no conflicts of interest. 39. Jared Baeten from the University of Washington in the United States received over $70 million in grant support from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, USAID, and the United States National Institutes of Health for PrEP-related research. Gilead Sciences donated PrEP medication to his research unit without additional monetary support. This was deemed financially significant. 40. Suna Balkan from Médecins Sans Frontières in France declared no conflicts of interest. 41. Carlos Caceres from Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia in Peru coordinates a network for multidisciplinary studies in ARV-based HIV prevention, supported by WHO and UNAIDS. This was deemed financially non-significant. 42. Frank Chimbwandira from the Ministry of Health in Malawi declared no conflicts of interest. 43. Simon Collins from HIV i-Base in the United Kingdom declared no conflicts of interest. 44. Frances Cowan from University College London and CeSHHAR in Zimbabwe is the principal investigator for an ART prevention trial among female sex workers in Zimbabwe. Gilead donated drugs for PrEP. This was deemed non-financially significant.
